text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Massive bid to find conversion bill compromise.
- 15 Palestinians injured in Hebron riots.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu looking to dump Finance Minister Meridor.
- Main opposition Labour party leader Barak to send team to London to study Blair's style.
- Soldier killed, three wounded in Lebanon.
- Infrastructure Minister Sharon willing to negotiate with Jewish National Fund on land reform blueprint.
- Soros increases Indigo stake.
- Rockwell Semiconductor Systems to expand local R&D centres.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu: In a year we'll lift most restrictions on foreign currency.
- Netanyahu insiders: He would not be sorry if Meridor resigned.
- Netanyahu: renewal of the negotiations with the Palestinians only if goal is final settlement.
MAARIV
- The drama around the economic plan: Meridor wants a decision by the government.
- Man took out a loan for $440 and has to pay back $73 million.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Ministerial front forming against Netanyahu's stand on economic plan.
GLOBES
- The basket sags about 0.6 percent below the trading band.
